Article Title: 'There are no unplayable deliveries': Gautam Gambhir raises 'concern' after India's batting horror show
Article Text:
Gautam Gambhir

India head coach Gautam Gambhir admitted that the team's batting failures were a major concern after their humiliating 244-run defeat against New Zealand in the fourth ODI, but insisted that the batters needed to find ways to counter challenging conditions.India were bundled out for just 89 while chasing 334, suffering their second-biggest defeat by runs in ODI cricket. Matt Henry led New Zealand's demolition job with a sensational six-wicket haul, exposing India's vulnerability against seam movement and disciplined bowling.Asked about India's struggles against the wobble seam, Gambhir chose not to get into the technical aspects of batting, instead putting the responsibility on the batters to adapt."I don’t go into technicality. There wasn’t a lot of deviation, its job of batter to negate movement. More than seam, areas and length created problems for us. We got stuck into the crease," Gambhir said during the post-match press conference.The India head coach also pointed out that the team's batting collapses were becoming a recurring concern. India had lost seven wickets for 111 in the previous game as well, and Gambhir stressed the need for the players to be better prepared both mentally and technically."Even last game we were 7 down for 111 it is a bit of concern. We need to be mentally, skill wise ready. 35-40/0 is fine in conditions like these. We have experience and can hopefully adapt in the last game," he said.Gambhir further refused to describe Henry's deliveries as unplayable, maintaining that India's experienced batting line-up should have been capable of dealing with the New Zealand pacer's challenge."There are no unplayable deliveries in international cricket. Matt Henry bowled in good areas but we should be able to negate that. You are always concerned when you get bundled out for 90 odd. These are conditions close to World Cup. Even previous game we lost seven wickets, its a concern," he added.Henry's opening over set the tone for India's collapse as Rohit Sharma , Virat Kohli and Shreyas Iyer were dismissed without scoring. Kyle Jamieson then removed Ruturaj Gaikwad, leaving India reeling at 9/4.Ishan Kishan and Axar Patel briefly resisted with a 44-run partnership, but Henry returned to dismiss Kishan and finish with figures of 6/27.Gambhir also reflected on India's missed opportunities in the field, particularly the chances offered by New Zealand centurion Will Young. The batter was dropped twice early in his innings before going on to score 125, helping the visitors post 333.The India coach also felt that Auqib Nabi was unfortunate not to dismiss Young, but acknowledged that dropped catches ultimately proved costly."Auqib Nabi was unlucky, had we got Will Young it could have been different. There’s always hindsight. We dropped catches and will have to pay for it," Gambhir said.Despite the heavy defeat, India remain 2-1 ahead in the five-match series. The fifth and final ODI on Sunday will decide the series, with Gambhir hoping his experienced batting unit can respond after two consecutive games in which the team has suffered significant middle-order and lower-order collapses.
Article Summary: India coach Gautam Gambhir admits team's batting failures are a major concern. India lost by 244 runs to New Zealand in the fourth ODI in Wellington. India were bundled out for just 89 while chasing 334, suffering their second-biggest defeat by runs in ODI cricket.

Article Title: IND vs NZ 4th ODI: 9/4 again! Team India suffer 1983 World Cup deja vu after 43 years
Article Text:

24/4 against New Zealand at Old Trafford in the 2019 World Cup

26/4 against New Zealand in Mount Maunganui, 2026

Rohit and Kohli register ducks together for only the second time

India vs New Zealand , Mount Maunganui, 2026

India's batting collapse against New Zealand brought back memories of one of the most famous moments in their cricket history. Forty-three years after being reduced to 9/4 against Zimbabwe in the 1983 World Cup, India suffered the same score in the fourth ODI at Bay Oval in Mount Maunganui on Friday.Chasing 334, India lost their first three wickets without scoring a run. Matt Henry struck with the very first ball of the innings, dismissing Rohit Sharma, before removing Virat Kohli and captain Shreyas Iyer in the same over.Rohit was caught by Finn Allen at first slip, Kohli was bowled while trying to defend a delivery that came back in, and Iyer was trapped LBW after New Zealand successfully reviewed the decision.The damage did not stop there. Ruturaj Gaikwad was dismissed for five, leaving India struggling at 9/4.The 1983 World Cup match against Zimbabwe at Tunbridge Wells is remembered for Kapil Dev's remarkable 175 not out. India were in deep trouble at 17/5 before their captain produced one of the greatest innings in World Cup history to rescue the team.On Friday, India were once again reduced to 9/4. It was only the second time that India had lost their first four wickets for fewer than 10 runs in an ODI.The first instance was the famous collapse against Zimbabwe in 1983.India's lowest scores in first 10 overs since 2018India's 26/4 in the first 10 overs against New Zealand was their lowest score in this period since 2018.Henry has troubled India in previous matches too. He took 2/10 in Wellington in 2019 and 3/13 against India at Old Trafford during the 2019 World Cup. On Friday, he took 3/14 during India's early collapse.Rohit and Kohli both failed to open their accounts against New Zealand. It was only the second time in their ODI careers that both had been dismissed for zero in the same match.The first instance came against Sri Lanka in Dambulla in 2010. The second was on Friday in Mount Maunganui.Henry has dismissed both Rohit and Kohli three times in ODIs. Rohit has scored 57 runs off 71 balls against the New Zealand pacer, averaging 19 at a strike rate of 80.28.Kohli has made 59 runs off 60 balls against Henry. He averages 19.67, with a strike rate of 98.33.Rohit joins list of Indian batters dismissed off the first ballRohit was out on the first ball of India's innings. He became only the latest Indian batter to suffer this dismissal. Sourav Ganguly and Virender Sehwag hold the unwanted record of being dismissed off the first ball of an ODI innings three times each.Sunil Gavaskar, Ravi Shastri, Kris Srikkanth, Manoj Prabhakar and Rohit have suffered the same fate once each.India also joined a list of teams that have lost their first three wickets without putting a run on the board in an ODI.
Article Summary: India lost their first three wickets without scoring a run against New Zealand. Matt Henry struck with the very first ball of the innings, dismissing Rohit Sharma, before removing Virat Kohli and Shreyas Iyer in the same over. It was only the second time in their ODI careers that both Rohit and Kohli had been dismissed for zero.

Article Title: PT Usha keeps fight alive, re-enters IOA election fray via National Sports Federation route
Article Text:
PT Usha (PTI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: PT Usha has refused to leave the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) presidential race without waging one last fight. After losing out on a direct entry into the IOA General Assembly by finishing fifth in Monday’s contentious Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit (SOM) elections and missing the four women’s places, Usha has found an unlikely ally in the the Ice Hockey Association of India (IHAI), as their women’s representative.Adopting the National Sports Federation (NSF) route, Usha is the IHAI’s women’s nominee in the provisional electoral college for the IOA Executive Council (EC) elections on Dec 5, released by electoral officer Sanjay K Srivastava on Thursday. Harjinder Singh is the association’s male nominee. The move is a pointed response to those who believed her SOM defeat had ended her bid for a second term as IOA chief.The SOM setback had triggered a protest from Usha. She lodged four complaints with the electoral officer over alleged campaigning by incumbent officials, messages seeking confirmation of voters’ participation and references to the sports ministry. In a Nov 9 letter to International Olympic Committee (IOC) president Kirsty Coventry, she sought an independent examination and asked whether govt or external influence had been exerted.The provisional list has its own flashpoints. At the All India Tennis Association (AITA), interim president Chintan Parikh and Rushmi Chakravarthi figure as representatives, but IOA’s current EC member Rohit Rajpal is missing.Rajpal has objected, alleging Parikh bypassed an AITA executive committee meeting and secured approval through an advisory group. He questioned why Leander Paes was not included and Parikh’s name sent instead. Both Rajpal and Parikh are contesting AITA’s elections on Nov 27 as presidential hopefuls.Another issue is at the Indian Weightlifting Federation (IWLF), where its president Sahdev Yadav has nominated himself as male representative and his wife, Sabina Yadav, as the female nominee.Former Athletics Federation of India (AFI) chief Adille Sumariwalla, who withdrew from the SOM contest, is back alongside Jyotirmoyee Sikdar, and remains an aspiring canidate for IOA’s top post. Former IOA secretary general Rajeev Mehta and NRAI’s Ajay Patel also feature, signalling an old-guard return.Hockey India’s list includes secretary general Bhola Nath Singh and Joydeep Kaur, but not HI president Dilip Tirkey, amid the power struggle for control of the federation between Singh and Tirkey. AIFF has nominated president Kalyan Chaubey, while the handball federation has proposed Udit Sheth, whose Yogasana Bharat recognition was quashed by the Delhi High Court.The final electoral roll will be published on Nov 15 after scrutiny and withdrawals. It will also include eight elected SOMs and India’s IOC member.
Article Summary: PT Usha has found an unlikely ally in the the Ice Hockey Association of India (IHAI), as their women’s representative. The move is a pointed response to those who believed her SOM defeat had ended her bid for a second term as IOA chief. She lodged four complaints with the electoral officer over alleged campaigning.

Article Title: Rs 50 lakh debt, visa nightmare: Teenage Indian chess prodigy risks losing US scholarship
Article Text:
IM Md Imran (Special Arrangements)

The Bratislava incident that changed everything

A university dream on hold

A family stretched to its financial limits

A race against time

NEW DELHI: Last June, seventeen-year-old Md Imran was in Bratislava, Slovakia, when an incident turned his European chess campaign into a nightmare. As previously reported on TimesofIndia.com , he lost his passport, his phone, money and several personal belongings. More than just his valuables, he had lost something far more important, his valid US F-1 visa and Schengen visa.Stranded in a foreign country, with no easy way to get home or continue his journey, the young Indian chess player suddenly found himself fighting a battle that had little to do with the 64 squares. But Imran, hailing from Andhra Pradesh, refused to let the setback end his journey.In the days and weeks that followed, he produced two consecutive Grandmaster (GM) norms, bringing him within touching distance of the coveted Grandmaster title.Yet, four months after that incident, Imran is back in India, facing a different kind of situation, which includes an unresolved US visa crisis, mounting family debt, and the possibility of losing a full university scholarship that could change his life.The teenager, who became an International Master (IM) in 2025, has already deferred his admission to the University of Texas at Rio Grande Valley (UTRGV) in Brownsville, Texas, from Fall 2026 to Spring 2027.His new university orientation is scheduled for January 19, 2027. If he cannot secure his US F-1 visa before then, he risks losing the scholarship altogether.For a teenager who has spent years travelling across continents to chase his Grandmaster dream, the next few months could prove decisive.The consequences of losing his passport in Bratislava were particularly severe because it contained both his valid US F-1 visa and his Schengen visa, which was valid until October 31.He eventually managed to obtain a replacement passport from the Indian Embassy in Budapest on June 29 and returned to India on July 6. But coming home did not mean the troubles were over."The very next day, on July 7th, I applied for a new Schengen visa for Hungary. This marked my 13th attempt at applying for a Schengen visa," Imran told TimesofIndia.com.Despite having competed extensively in Hungary over the previous two years, and having previously received a one-year multiple-entry visa from the same consulate, Imran was granted only a three-month visa, valid from July 18 to October 31.The decision left him frustrated, particularly when he knew fellow players who had received visas valid for two to five years in far fewer attempts."It sounded completely ridiculous, especially when I know many friends who have received 2- to 5-year validity visas in just their 2nd to 5th attempts. I truly don't understand what's wrong with my case," he added.For a young professional chess player, travelling back to India solely to process visas means more than another appointment and a few documents."Flying back to India solely for visa processing costs an exorbitant amount of time and heavy money on flight tickets, on top of the constant re-application hurdles," he added.Even amid the uncertainty, Imran had already earned two norms in closed round-robin tournaments and was chasing his final open Swiss GM norm to complete the requirements for the Grandmaster title.His original plan was to continue competing in Europe, secure the remaining norm and return to India in time to obtain a US visa and attend UTRGV's Fall 2026 student orientation on August 23. But the US visa appointment never materialised."I waited in Europe and tried for a U.S. appointment all the way through August, September, and October. Unfortunately, despite trying every single day for four months since the June incident, I still have not secured an appointment," he said.With the August university deadline passing, he had little choice but to defer his admission to Spring 2027.His scholarship remains at stake. If he cannot make it to the university by the January 19 orientation, he could lose the financial support that would help him pursue higher education alongside his chess career.Between July and October, he competed in over ten events. However, only three were strong open tournaments where he had a realistic opportunity to secure his final GM norm.The remaining events were regular prize-money opens and round-robin competitions that helped him stay active.The three major opportunities were also poorly spaced, with two tournaments scheduled back-to-back between August 8 and 23, followed by the final one from October 3 to 11.It was a relentless schedule, made even harder by the uncertainty surrounding his university admission and his inability to secure a US visa appointment.The pressure eventually took its toll on the chessboard."Under the intense psychological pressure of the missing norm and my crumbling U.S. visa situation, my performance dipped. I suffered an insane rating decline despite relentless fighting spirit. Completely exhausted and under immense stress, I flew back home on October 12," Imran, who had a peak rating of 2503 and is now rated 2477, revealed.Imran's father is a police officer, while his mother is a homemaker. Coming from a middle-class background, the family has had to stretch its resources to support his international chess career.Playing professionally in Europe costs between Rs 1.5 lakh and Rs 3 lakh every month. The expenses include flights, visas, accommodation, tournament entry fees, food and travel between countries.The family has reportedly accumulated loans of around Rs 40-50 lakh to finance his career. The June incident in Slovakia added another unexpected financial burden, with the loss of his passport, phone and other valuables."My father has supported me with everything he possibly can, stretching himself to the absolute limit, but it's falling short over time," Imran further noted. "I built my chess career entirely through my own hard work without formal high-end coaching."Imran has approached the Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister's Office and other political leaders, seeking financial assistance through state sports incentive schemes. However, his requests have so far gone unanswered.With his three-month Schengen visa approaching its October 31 expiry, Imran returned to the Hungarian Consulate in Mumbai on October 16 for another application. It was his 14th Schengen visa application.This time, he received an emergency appointment and was granted a one-year visa on October 24. While the longer validity offers some relief, it was still shorter than the five-year visa he had hoped to secure given his extensive tournament and travel history across Europe.At least one part of the travel crisis had eased. But the bigger problem remained untouched, his US F-1 visa. With January 19, 2027, approaching, Imran now needs to secure an appointment and complete the visa process in time to join UTRGV and protect his scholarship.Despite everything, Imran is preparing to return to Europe for another demanding tournament circuit in the hope of securing his final GM norm. He is scheduled to fly back on November 19, with four events lined up across Portugal, Spain and Sweden:The schedule leaves little room for rest. More importantly, he is desperately hoping to secure a US visa appointment before leaving India on November 19."My life is currently at a critical crossroads. Between the heavy financial debts of playing professional chess, the constant struggle to secure my final GM norm, and the looming threat of losing my U.S. university scholarship at the University of Texas at Rio Grande Valley if I can't resolve my visa crisis by Spring 2027, the situation is completely overwhelming," he concluded.For a teenager who has done so much to keep his dreams alive, the question is whether the support he needs will arrive before January 19.
Article Summary: Indian chess player Md Imran was in Bratislava, Slovakia, when an incident turned his European chess campaign into a nightmare. He lost his passport, his phone, money and several personal belongings. He also lost his valid US F-1 visa and Schengen visa. Four months after that incident, Imran is back in India, facing a different kind of situation, which includes an unresolved US visa crisis.

Article Title: ‘Very disappointed’: IOC backs call for clean IOA elections after Usha flags SOM poll irregularities; warns of damage to India’s Olympic reputation
Article Text:
PT Usha (PTI Photo)

NEW DELHI: The International Olympic Committee (IOC) has stepped into the raging Indian Olympic Association (IOA) election controversy, expressing strong displeasure over the recurring disputes surrounding its electoral process and warning that the developments are damaging the reputation of the Olympic movement in India.In a strongly worded communication to IOA president PT Usha on her complaints, the world body has called for elections to be conducted in strict compliance with the Olympic Charter and IOA Constitution, in a “free and fair manner and without any external interference”.The IOC's letter to Usha, in the exclusive possession of TOI, comes in the wake of the IOA president's Nov 9 communication to IOC president Kirsty Coventry, in which she sought an independent examination of alleged irregularities in the contentious Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit (SOM) elections. The latest communication, signed by James Macleod, Director, NOC Relations, Olympic Solidarity and Olympism365, has also been marked to IOC member Nita Ambani and the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA).Opening with an unambiguous expression of displeasure, Macleod wrote: “In response to the complaints and media reports that have been brought to our attention over the past few days, we would like to express the IOC’s position as follows.”The IOC then made its disappointment explicit, stating: “The IOC is very disappointed to note that, once again, issues and disputes seem to have resurfaced in the conduct of the IOA election process and in the implementation of the rules governing the IOA elections, despite all the efforts made over the past few years to establish a strong governance framework for the IOA in accordance with the Olympic Charter and the Basic Principles of Good Governance within the Olympic Movement. ”In perhaps its strongest observation, the IOC warned that the controversy was having consequences beyond the IOA's internal power struggle. “This extremely regrettable situation is, once again, negatively affecting the operations and reputation of the Olympic Movement in India,” the letter stated.The IOC's intervention assumes significance against the backdrop of Usha's detailed complaint to Coventry. In her three-page communication, the IOA president had flagged alleged campaigning by incumbent officials, WhatsApp messages soliciting votes for a particular panel, communications seeking confirmation of voters' participation and references to the sports ministry during an election involving a secret ballot.She had also questioned the handling of four representations submitted to electoral officer Sanjay K. Srivastava and sought an independent examination of whether government or external influence had been exerted.Usha had maintained that her complaint was not an attempt to challenge the result simply because she had lost, but was about the conduct and oversight of the electoral process and the need to protect the autonomy of the IOA.The IOC has now directly addressed the responsibility of those conducting the elections. “We urge the IOA and the Electoral Officer directly responsible for the IOA election process to ensure that the IOA elections can be conducted in full compliance with the Olympic Charter, the IOA Constitution, and all applicable rules, in a free and fair manner and without any external interference,” Macleod wrote.The letter further stressed: “We sincerely count on everyone's collaboration to ensure that the above is strictly respected, in order to avoid any unnecessary complications and further escalation.” It also requested that a copy be sent to the relevant government authorities.The controversy erupted after Usha finished fifth with 40 votes in the six-way contest for four women's SOM positions on November 9. Anju Bobby George topped the poll with 53 votes, followed by Rani Rampal (50), Dola Banerjee (45) and Saina Nehwal (43).While the IOC has not adjudicated Usha's specific allegations or named anyone responsible for the reported violations, its unequivocal warning puts the IOA's electoral administration under international scrutiny.With the executive council elections scheduled for Dec 5, the message is unmistakable: the process must command credibility, follow the rules and remain free from external interference.
Article Summary: The International Olympic Committee (IOC) has stepped into the raging Indian Olympic Association (IOA) election controversy. In a strongly worded communication to IOA president PT Usha on her complaints, the world body has called for elections to be conducted in strict compliance with the Olympic Charter and IOA Constitution. The IOC warned that the controversy was having consequences beyond the IOA's internal power struggle.

Pune: There was a lot of history riding on Vivaan Kapoor when he was shooting for gold in the men's trap event at the ISSF World Championships in Doha on Thursday.The Jaipur shooter missed creating some, while still becoming part of history, as he clinched silver and an Olympic quota for the Los Angeles Games. Vivaan, 24, became only the fourth Indian to win a World Championships medal in trap and only second after Karni Singh to win a silver.Manavjit Singh Sandhu is the only Indian to have won gold in the event at the Worlds, while Zoravar Singh Sandhu's bronze is the other medal India has won in this category.It was also the first time when two Indians entered a trap final in the World Championships. Other than Vivaan, Udaivir Singh Jaijee also entered the 8-man final, finishing sixth.In the final, Vivaan was in excellent form as he shot 29 clay out of 30. He was tied at 29 with Kuwait's Abdulrahman Al-Faihan as the match progressed to the shoot-off. Vivaan looked good in the shoot-off, but the Kuwaiti shooter too didn't budge and beat the Indian by one shot taking the shoot-off 3-2. The final was a strong field as it had Paris Games gold medallist Nathan Hales and silver medallist Ying Qi of China. While Qi took bronze with 22 hits, Hales got eliminated at the fifth position with the score of 11.Udaivir finished sixth with 11 hits.Earlier, in the qualification round, Vivaan and Udaivir faced a 7-way tie as seven shooters were tied at the score of 120. They faced the shoot-off for four spots and both Indians cleared the hurdle to get into the top-.
Article Summary: Vivaan Kapoor won silver in the men's trap event at the ISSF World Championships in Doha. The Jaipur shooter clinched silver and an Olympic quota for the Los Angeles Games. Vivaan, 24, became only the fourth Indian to win a World Championships medal in trap.

Article Title: 'That medal was the only prize we got for winning Olympics': MM Somaya
Article Text:
MM Somaya

(Former

Indian hockey

captain

MM Somaya

is an 1980 Olympic gold medallist and 1982 Asian Games silver medallist. He spoke to Manuja Veerappa).

That week we were in our home in Kodagu, a little away from Madikeri town. By the time I returned from my morning walk that day (Oct 28), our neighbours in Bengaluru had called my wife to inform her about a break-in at our place.My first thought was about my medals, especially the 1980 Moscow Olympics gold, because those were the only precious items which I felt we had left at home. As my wife drove us to Bengaluru, I spent much of the journey calling my niece and then the police, who put me at ease by telling me not to panic.As the police worked on collecting fingerprints and other forensic evidence, I kept asking my family who had gone in what they could actually see. The medal boxes were there, they said, but the medals were missing. I hoped they were under the pile of clothes those people had strewn and left behind.My heart sank when I walked into the house. First, at all the clothes all around the place, then at the broken cupboard lock. The empty boxes of medals made me feel very sad and disappointed because I cherished them so much; they carried so many good memories and sentiments, and to me, they will always be priceless.I remember when I came back from Moscow, people often asked about the medal. But over time, fewer people asked to see it. Maybe the importance of Olympic sports had declined as other sports took over, but somehow, all that didn't matter at this moment.My worst fear was losing the medals and never seeing them again. And that would have been a big blow because they were the only prize we received for winning and participating in the Olympics at Moscow. I felt a great dread that I wouldn't get them back and that they wouldn't be recovered.As I have said before, I thought the people who took it away likely didn't know its sporting value. For me, it was priceless, for them, it was gold. It could end up at a pawn shop or worse, just be melted down. That thought gnawed away inside me.Despite the sinking feeling, I immediately began running other scenarios through my mind - whether I could apply to the International Olympic Committee for a replacement medal because of the loss. At the same time, there was that smidgen of hope that lingered because the police had given me their assurance.In the two weeks between the break-in and Wednesday's recovery, I was assailed by a lot of nostalgia. The day we won the medal, Zafar Iqbal and I were taken for a dope test immediately after the medal ceremony. Once back in the Games Village, I was so exhausted that I slept without changing. The medal had stayed around my neck! Other memories played out as well.I thought back with gratitude because that was my first time playing for India. Also, I had never been out of the country. I had never played on artificial turf before. I looked back at the youngster in me, who wore an oversized India kit (I was a thin boy) and went out to play.Days with our coach, Balkrishan Singh, and captain V Baskaran came back to me, and recollections of how they had faith in me and guided me. I wasn't in the initial playing XI and was one of the two substitutes, more like an understudy. Just before the Olympics, we played a few practice matches against the local clubs, and Balkrishan sir and Baskaran felt I should be in the playing XI, which I'd never dreamt I would be in. It's where my career took off. The trust they showed in me meant I probably never sat on the bench for almost nine years that followed.
Article Summary: MM Somaya is an 1980 Olympic gold medallist and 1982 Asian Games silver medalist. His medals were stolen during a break-in at his home in Kodagu, Karnataka. The medals were the only prize we received for winning and participating in the Olympics at Moscow.

NEW DELHI: New Zealand have been forced into another squad reshuffle ahead of the third ODI against India, with mounting injury concerns threatening to disrupt their plans for the remainder of the series.Fast bowler Kristian Clarke has been called up as cover for Blair Tickner ahead of Tuesday's third ODI, while Lockie Ferguson has been ruled out of the fourth and fifth matches after failing to recover fully from a calf injury sustained during the T20I series.The latest developments add to New Zealand's growing list of fitness concerns, with Matt Henry also recovering from a concussion-related issue and Tickner required to undergo a mandatory stand-down period despite being cleared of concussion.Ferguson has been ruled out of the final two ODIs after failing to recover fully from a low-grade tear in his right calf. Legendary India batter Sunil Gavaskar has weighed in on the debate surrounding Virat Kohli 's pursuit of 100 international centuries, suggesting that a teammate making a personal sacrifice to help the star reach the landmark would bring joy to Indian cricket fans as well.Kohli was in superb touch during the first ODI against New Zealand, smashing 74 off just 51 deliveries to guide India towards victory in a low-scoring contest. However, Gavaskar raised an interesting possibility in his latest column for: had Kohli stayed at the crease for longer, captain Shubman Gill and vice-captain Shreyas Iyer could have found themselves in a difficult position.With India closing in on the target, the two batters might have had to choose between finishing the match quickly and giving Kohli an opportunity to reach his century. The prospect becomes even more significant given that Kohli is chasing the historic mark of 100 international hundreds.Gavaskar acknowledged that winning a match must remain the team's primary objective, but argued that helping a player achieve such a landmark, provided it does not compromise the result, could be a moment of collective celebration."Indians have always been fond of records and so there's always a debate about the rights and wrongs of going for it.One thing for sure that 99% of those who say they don't play for records are actually incapable talent and temperament wise of setting any and so it's easy for them to say so," Gavaskar wrote."There is not a single Indian cricket fan who does not want Kohli to get to 100 international centuries. We are all cheering for him to get there and so, if there's an occasion where some other teammate sacrifices his runs to allow him the chance to get there, the glory will not be just Kohli's but for all Indian cricket fans too," he added.Kohli eventually fell for 74 with India at 124/3 in the rain-affected contest, leaving the team with relatively little work to do in the chase. His dismissal also meant Gill and Iyer did not have to confront the possibility of managing the chase around his personal milestone.Gavaskar felt the two players were spared a potentially awkward situation, including the prospect of facing criticism from fans on social media if India had delayed sealing the victory to give Kohli a chance to complete his hundred."Kohli got out in the 70s. Gill and Iyer were thus spared any blowback if the winning runs had been hit with Kohli unbeaten in the 90s. Yes, it's a team game, but it's also good for the team if one of its members, especially a star player, gets to a personal milestone without affecting the team's chances of winning," Gavaskar pointed out.Kohli, who now plays only ODIs, has 86 international centuries to his name. He is chasing a landmark that remains exclusive to Sachin Tendulkar, the only batter to have scored 100 international hundreds.
Article Summary: Virat Kohli is chasing the historic mark of 100 international hundreds. Sunil Gavaskar says a teammate making a personal sacrifice to help the star reach the landmark would bring joy to Indian cricket fans as well. Kohli was in superb touch during the first ODI against New Zealand, smashing 74.

Former India cricketer Ajay Jadeja has praised Arshdeep Singh's overall performance in India's five-wicket victory over New Zealand in the first ODI in Auckland, but believes the left-arm pacer could have avoided an expensive finish to his spell.India began their five-match ODI series with a comfortable win at Eden Park on Wednesday, November 4. In a rain-interrupted contest reduced to 32 overs per side, New Zealand were bowled out for 185 before India chased down the revised target of 143 in just 22.4 overs. Virat Kohli led the chase with a fluent 74, while Shubman Gill contributed 37 as the duo stitched together a 113-run partnership. India eventually crossed the finish line with five wickets to spare and 56 deliveries remaining.With the ball, Arshdeep was India's leading wicket-taker, claiming four wickets in his 10 overs. However, his figures of 4/70 were inflated by an expensive final over in which New Zealand tailender Blair Tickner struck him for three sixes, taking 23 runs off the over.Assessing the pacer's performance, Jadeja felt Arshdeep had been impressive for most of his spell but allowed the opportunity to complete a five-wicket haul to influence his bowling towards the end."I would call him slightly greedy. He himself said that as well. If you remove his last over, he had dismissed four batters before that and had given 40-odd runs. He got slightly greedy for the fifth wicket in the last over," Jadeja said on Sony Sports Network.Arshdeep had himself admitted after the match that the fifth wicket would have been his favourite, indicating that he was keen to complete a five-wicket haul. Despite missing out on the milestone, his four-wicket effort placed him in an exclusive group of Indian fast bowlers to achieve the feat in an ODI in New Zealand, alongside Javagal Srinath and Mohammed Shami.Jadeja, however, stressed that the expensive final over should not overshadow what Arshdeep brings to India's bowling combination. He pointed to the value of having a left-arm fast bowler in an attack that already features Jasprit Bumrah, adding that the competition for places would only benefit the team."It happens. It's natural, but Arshdeep Singh is showing that he can play in ODIs as well, which I believe is a very good thing when a left-arm seamer gets added to this attack with (Jasprit) Bumrah. The competition has increased a lot, which is very good for India," Jadeja elaborated.Jadeja also reserved praise for Anshul Kamboj, who delivered an economical spell of 2/22 from his 10 overs and walked away with the Player of the Match award.The former India batter acknowledged that Kamboj had faced questions over his bowling during his Test debut against England in 2025, particularly regarding his pace and tendency to bowl no-balls. However, he felt the youngster had shown considerable improvement in Auckland.Jadeja also suggested that Kamboj's workload before the England assignment could have contributed to his struggles, pointing out that fatigue can affect a bowler's execution. His performance against New Zealand, according to Jadeja, reflected better pace, consistency and accuracy."He bowled extremely well. The vision everyone had was that he didn't have pace when he played in England and was bowling a lot of no-balls. I think he had come after playing a lot of cricket then. So a guy also gets tired. It's not that easy. Then he was playing for the first time, but the consistency and the slight increase in his pace he showed today (Wednesday), if we talk about the accuracy amongst the four bowlers, it's Anshul Kamboj," Jadeja added.
Article Summary: India beat New Zealand by five wickets in the first ODI in Auckland. Ajay Jadeja praised Arshdeep Singh's performance, but said he could have avoided expensive final over. Jadeja also praised Anshul Kamboj's bowling, saying he had shown improvement.

Australia's 21-year-old pacer Mahli Beardman made a dream start to his international career, tearing through England's batting line-up to claim six wickets on his ODI debut in Perth on Friday. With figures of 6/24, Beardman became the first Australian male fast bowler to take a six-wicket haul on ODI debut, breaking a record that had stood for 38 years.Beardman also became only the second Australian male bowler to take five or more wickets in his first ODI as England were bowled out for just 131 in the series opener.The young pacer struck early, removing England captain Harry Brook before sending Joe Root back to the pavilion. NEW DELHI: India suffered a shocking start to their chase of 334 against New Zealand in the fourth ODI at Bay Oval in Mount Maunganui on Friday. Rohit Sharma Virat Kohli and captain Shreyas Iyer all returned to the pavilion without scoring. New Zealand pacer Matt Henry dismissed all three batters in the opening over to leave India reeling at 0/3.Henry opened the bowling for New Zealand and struck with his very first delivery. He then removed Kohli on the fifth ball before sending Iyer back on the final delivery of the over.It was a triple-wicket maiden for Henry, who gave New Zealand the perfect start after the hosts had posted 333.Henry got Rohit Sharma with the first ball of the innings. The New Zealand pacer bowled a short-of-a-good-length delivery that moved away from the right-hander and also produced extra bounce. Rohit was forced to play at it and got a thick outside edge. Finn Allen took a simple catch at first slip. Rohit walked back after facing just one ball, registering a golden duck.Henry struck again on the fifth ball of the over to remove Virat Kohli. After bowling deliveries that moved away from the batter, Henry brought one back sharply into Kohli. The ball stayed a little low as Kohli tried to defend it towards the leg-side.Kohli was unable to deal with the inward movement. The ball went through the gap between his bat and pad and hit the stumps. Kohli was bowled for a four-ball duck, leaving India at 0/2.Henry completed a stunning over by dismissing India captain Shreyas Iyer on the final delivery. The pacer bowled a sharp delivery that came back into Iyer. The batter tried to defend it but missed the ball, which hit him on the back leg.Umpire Kumar Dharmasena initially turned down the appeal. New Zealand took a review, and ball-tracking showed three reds, confirming that the ball would have hit the middle stump.Iyer was given out LBW for a first-ball duck. Henry had completed a triple-wicket maiden, with India losing their first three wickets without scoring a run.This was only the second time that Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli had both scored ducks in the same ODI.The previous instance came against Sri Lanka in Dambulla in 2010. That match is also remembered for the controversial incident in which Virender Sehwag was denied a century after Suraj Randiv bowled a no-ball when Sehwag was on 99 not out. Sehwag hit the delivery for six, but the run did not count.India became the fifth team to lose their first three wickets without scoring a run in an ODI.
Article Summary: India lose first three wickets without scoring a run in fourth ODI against New Zealand. Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli and Shreyas Iyer all returned to the pavilion without scoring. New Zealand pacer Matt Henry dismissed all three batters in the opening over to leave India reeling at 0/3.

Former Australia opener David Warner has continued to back Usman Khawaja following his explosive claims about the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, also known as Sandpapergate. A few hours after Australia captain Pat Cummins addressed the allegations at a news conference in Sydney, Warner accused him of throwing Khawaja under the bus.Warner, who was handed a 12-month ban for his role in the 2018 scandal, backed Khawaja's version of events in his autobiography, Sabr. Khawaja has claimed that all members of the Test team knew about the use of sandpaper during the Cape Town Test against South Africa.This contradicts Cummins' public statements. It is the truth and I really, really support him.“I actually feel for him at the moment. I actually feel that the captain today actually threw Uzzie under the bus. And I'm very, very disappointed about that.”Warner also repeated his criticism of the investigation into the scandal, describing it as "botched."Cummins held a news conference at the Sydney Cricket Ground on Friday, hours before Australia's home-season opening ODI against England in Perth.He said he was ready to answer questions for as long as required because he wanted to put the controversy behind him.Khawaja's autobiography has brought the eight-year-old scandal back into the spotlight. In the book, he claimed that the entire team knew about the ball-tampering plan.Cummins, who was part of Australia's bowling attack in the Cape Town Test, strongly rejected the claim.“When he says we all knew, if by that he means that we knew sandpaper was going out in the field, he's 100% wrong,” Cummins said. “I've said that consistently for the last eight years. Article Title: Best ever! From 14 medals to 114: How India achieved more with fewer athletes at the Asian Para Games
Article Text:

From 14 medals in 2010 to 114 in 2026, India’s remarkable rise continued in Aichi-Nagoya as a smaller contingent surpassed its previous best, achieved 30 gold medals and secured its highest-ever finish at the continental para-sport showpiece.India’s campaign at the Asian Para Games 2026 was a triumph that few would have predicted when the size of the contingent became known. With just 167 athletes travelling to Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, the prospect of repeating the 100-plus medal haul achieved at Hangzhou in 2023 appeared ambitious. The previous edition had seen India send more than 300 athletes to the competition, returning with a record 108 medals after subsequent revisions to the original tally.But the Indian contingent defied expectations, producing an even bigger return with significantly fewer athletes. India finished the fifth edition of the Asian Para Games with 114 medals — 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze — to secure fourth place, both the highest medal tally and the best finish in the country's history at the event.The numbers tell a compelling story of progress. India improved its medal tally for the fifth consecutive edition, added to its gold-medal record and finished ahead of South Korea, which had threatened to challenge its position in the final standings.More than the record itself, the achievement highlighted how far India's para-sport movement has travelled in 16 years — from a modest 14-medal return at the inaugural edition in 2010 to a fourth-place finish among Asia's leading para-sport nations.India's progress at the Asian Para Games has been steady, with each edition bringing a new high in the overall medal tally.At Guangzhou in 2010, India won 14 medals — one gold, four silver and nine bronze — to finish 15th. The 2014 edition in Incheon brought a substantial improvement, with the country collecting 33 medals, including three gold, but remaining 15th in the standings.The breakthrough arrived at Jakarta in 2018. India's medal tally rose to 72, comprising 15 gold, 24 silver and 33 bronze, while its position improved to ninth.Hangzhou in 2023 marked another major leap. India crossed the 100-medal barrier for the first time, initially returning with 111 medals before the tally was revised to 108 following a doping-related disqualification and a medal reallocation. The revised haul comprised 27 gold, 32 silver and 49 bronze, with India eventually classified sixth.Aichi-Nagoya extended that upward trajectory. India added six medals to its revised Hangzhou total, increased its gold-medal count from 27 to 30 and climbed two places to fourth.The numbers at a glance: India's medal tally increased more than eightfold between 2010 and 2026. Its gold-medal count grew from one to 30, while its position improved from 15th to fourth.The rise has not been limited to the overall tally. India has improved its standing in three successive editions since 2014, moving from 15th to ninth, then sixth and now fourth. The 2026 result represents the culmination of a sustained upward trend rather than an isolated breakthrough.The most striking feature of India's latest performance was the efficiency with which its athletes converted participation into medals.India fielded 167 athletes — 111 men and 56 women — across 11 sports at Aichi-Nagoya. That was considerably fewer than the 309 athletes listed for the Hangzhou campaign in 2023, yet the team surpassed its previous best by six medals.The comparison is revealing. India sent approximately 46 per cent fewer athletes than it did to Hangzhou, but its medal tally increased by nearly six per cent. The gold-medal count rose by three, the silver tally by three, and the bronze count remained unchanged.On a simple medals-per-athlete measure, India's return increased from approximately 0.35 medals per athlete in Hangzhou to 0.68 in Aichi-Nagoya. This is an aggregate comparison, not an individual success rate, since athletes can win multiple medals and the number of events and opportunities varies across sports.Nevertheless, the figures underline the scale of the achievement. A smaller squad did not merely match the previous edition's success; it established a new benchmark for Indian para-sport.Para-athletics was the backbone of India's campaign, delivering 65 medals — 22 gold, 19 silver and 24 bronze. That represented nearly 57 per cent of the country's overall tally and made athletics the single biggest contributor to India's fourth-place finish.Para-badminton followed with 16 medals, including three gold, five silver and eight bronze. Together, athletics and badminton accounted for 81 medals, more than 70 per cent of India's total.Swimming contributed 11 medals, comprising three silver and eight bronze. Archery added six medals, including three gold and three silver, while shooting produced five, with two gold, two silver and one bronze.Athletics' contribution also illustrates how India's progress has accelerated. At Hangzhou, para-athletics produced 52 medals, including 16 gold, 17 silver and 19 bronze. In Aichi-Nagoya, the discipline's haul rose to 65, with six additional gold medals.Badminton's contribution was different. India won 21 medals in the sport at Hangzhou, including four gold, but finished with 16 in 2026. Instead, the substantial gains in athletics and the contributions from other sports helped compensate for the decline in badminton medals.That distinction matters: the record haul reflects both the strength of India's established medal-winning disciplines and the need to broaden its success across events in future editions.India's record was supported by athletes who delivered more than once during the competition. A total of 26 Indian athletes won multiple medals, while six athletes collected multiple gold medals, demonstrating the importance of individual excellence in a campaign involving 11 sports.Archer Sheetal Devi was among the standout performers, winning two gold medals and a silver. Her two golds came in the mixed compound and individual compound events, while the silver added to her three-medal haul.Athletics provided several other multiple gold medallists. Dilip Gavit, Nishad Kumar, Pranav Soorma and Simran Sharma each won two gold medals, while shooting contributed through Mona Agarwal, who also secured two golds.Four athletes finished with three medals apiece: Sheetal Devi in archery, Thulasimathi Murugesan in badminton, Ravi Budigina in swimming and Himanshu Nandal in swimming. Their performances illustrated how athletes winning across multiple events can make a significant difference to a country's final tally.The figures also invite comparison with Hangzhou, where 25 Indian athletes won multiple medals. The increase to 26 in 2026 was modest, but the overall tally improved despite a much smaller contingent. The result points to a campaign in which medal-winning performances were concentrated among a relatively small squad.India's rise at the Asian Para Games has coincided with a significant improvement at the Paralympics, strengthening the country's standing in international para-sport.At Rio 2016, India won four medals and finished 43rd. Tokyo 2020 marked a breakthrough, with 19 medals — five gold, eight silver and six bronze — lifting India to 24th. At Paris 2024, India recorded its best Paralympic haul of 29 medals, comprising seven gold, nine silver and 13 bronze, to finish 18th.The progression at the Paralympics mirrors the broader trend at the Asian Para Games: larger medal returns, more gold medals and improvements in the standings.India's able-bodied contingent had also finished fourth at the 2026 Asian Games, although its 85-medal tally was below the 106 medals achieved at Hangzhou in 2023. The para contingent's performance offered a contrasting story of growth, with its medal count rising and its position improving.China dominated Aichi-Nagoya, finishing with 435 medals, including 207 gold. Hosts Japan were second with 186 medals, while Uzbekistan finished third with 145. India placed fourth with 114, ahead of South Korea, which collected 100 medals, including 29 gold.India's final position was not guaranteed until the closing stages. South Korea remained within reach, but its final-day return of one gold and two silver left it one gold behind India. The Indian contingent held on to fourth place with 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze.The gap to third-placed Uzbekistan shows that further progress will require India to expand its medal-winning strength across disciplines. Yet the immediate achievement is significant: India has moved from 15th at the first two editions to fourth, while increasing its tally at every successive Games.The challenge now is to sustain that momentum, build a deeper pool of competitive athletes and reduce dependence on a handful of disciplines.For a contingent of just 167 athletes, 114 medals represent more than a record. They mark the latest step in a 16-year transformation of Indian para-sport — one that began with 14 medals in Guangzhou and has now culminated in a historic fourth-place finish in Aichi-Nagoya.
Article Summary: India fielded 167 athletes — 111 men and 56 women — across 11 sports at Aichi- Nagoya. India finished the fifth edition of the Asian Para Games with 114 medals — 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze — to secure fourth place. It is the best finish in the country's history at the event.

NEW DELHI: Suhas Yathiraj was disappointed with his bronze medal at the Asian Para Games in Nagoya. Having beaten Indonesia's Fredy Setiawan in their group match just days earlier, the Indian shuttler had hoped to reach the final and fight for gold.Suhas lost the men's singles SL4 semifinal 23-21, 8-21, 15-21. He had chances to take the opening game but failed to convert them. After bouncing back to win the second game 21-8, he lost focus at a crucial stage of the decider.“Definitely not satisfied with bronze. I think if I had played up to my full potential, I would have definitely done better. In fact, I defeated Fredy of Indonesia in the group match in Nagoya only a few days ago,” Suhas told TimesofIndia.com from Aichi-Nagoya in Japan.“In the semifinal match, the first set was very close. I lost 23-21 and I had game point, set point, but I couldn't convert that. In the second set, I won very easily. In the third set, I think after 10-all, I sort of lost focus for two to three rallies. That is where he took the game. So, it was not my best day, I would assume. I would always love to win a gold medal. So, yes, I am a little sad from that angle,” he said.The defeat also reminded him of how important it is to perform under pressure at major tournaments.“It is the most important factor to win medals at major games because you might be training well, you might actually have the fitness and the skills. But if you don't recreate that during the major games, then probably it is of not much use in terms of professional success,” Suhas said.Suhas, an IAS officer, said he had never imagined representing India in international badminton a decade ago.In November 2016, he made his debut at the Asian Championships in Beijing and won gold. Since then, he has won several medals at major international events. These include bronze at the 2018 Asian Para Games in Jakarta, silver at the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics, another silver at the Paris 2024 Paralympics, gold at the Hangzhou Asian Para Games and bronze in Nagoya.The 43-year-old has represented India at two Paralympic Games, Tokyo in 2020 and Paris in 2024, winning silver on both occasions.With the Los Angeles 2028 Paralympics approaching, the big question is whether he can go one step further and win gold.The desire is there, but Suhas is not looking too far ahead. He wants to take things one step at a time.“If you had asked me 10 years ago, I didn't even know that I would play for India. But whenever I look at the medals and the love I have got from fans and sportspersons around the world, the journey has been quite satisfying. I have had the honour of wearing the Indian jersey and winning medals for my country,” he said.“I am grateful for what God has given me. I never imagined that I would become an IAS officer one day, an Arjuna awardee or a badminton player winning medals for India. I never imagined all this. But thanks to the Almighty for all these,” Suhas, who is also an Arjuna Award recipient, said.“So if God and destiny have been kind to me, I hope they will take me to a place that I deserve. I hope I can do the best that I can in whatever I choose to,” he added.For most people, the end of a hectic working day is a time to relax, spend time with family, play with their children or watch a movie.For Suhas, it is often time to pick up his badminton racket and head to the court. His day includes early-morning gym sessions, office work, inspections, meetings, video conferences and checking files. Despite his demanding responsibilities as an IAS officer, he makes time for badminton and follows a strict fitness routine to compete at the highest level.Balancing the two careers is not easy, but his love for the sport keeps him going.“If you choose what you love, then the journey becomes painless. You enjoy that journey. That's what I do,” Suhas said.Explaining how he manages his work and training, he said: “It is challenging. My training generally starts in the night and it always involves sacrifices. Probably others would be spending time with their family members or having leisure time. My leisure time is to play badminton. In badminton, you need an extremely high level of fitness. It's challenging, hectic but at the same time I love it.”“I don't remember eating sweets in the last many months. I can't recall when I had my last sweet. So, I almost don't eat sweets or fried food and am also quite conscious about the nutrition that I take,” he said.Suhas grew up watching Malaysian badminton great Lee Chong Wei and was inspired by his movement on the court.“Yes, I have always been inspired by so many top players in the able-bodied category. Growing up, I watched the matches of Lee Chong Wei and how he used to move around the court,” he said.“Even in India, the top shuttlers perform extremely well, whether it is Lakshya Sen, HS Prannoy or Kidambi Srikanth. I know them personally and have always admired how well they are able to compete at the top,” Suhas signed off.

NEW DELHI: India signed off from the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Para Games with their best-ever medal haul of 114 medals as the week-long continental competition concluded with a closing ceremony at the Mizuho Park Athletics Stadium in Nagoya, Japan, on Saturday.Double gold medallists Nishad Kumar and Mona Agarwal led the Indian contingent as flag-bearers at the ceremony, marking the end of a landmark campaign in which the country's para-athletes delivered historic victories, world-record performances and podium sweeps across disciplines.India finished fourth in the overall standings with 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze medals, surpassing its previous best of 108 medals at the 2022 Hangzhou Games.Held in Japan for the first time, the fifth edition of the Asian Para Games brought together around 4,000 athletes and staff from 45 countries and regions. The competition featured 18 sports, with more than 20 world records reportedly set during the seven-day event.China topped the medal table with 435 medals, including 207 gold, while hosts Japan finished second with 186 medals — 64 gold, 60 silver and 62 bronze.Uzbekistan emerged as the third-ranked nation, collecting 145 medals, including 45 gold.India's fourth-place finish was particularly significant given the size of its contingent. A total of 168 para-athletes represented the country at Aichi-Nagoya, compared with 309 at the previous edition in Hangzhou.President Droupadi Murmu congratulated the Indian contingent on its record performance, saying the achievement reflected the athletes' hard work, perseverance and self-belief.In a post on X, Murmu said the unprecedented medal haul would inspire young people to dream big, work with dedication and remain positive in the face of challenges. He later added a silver medal in mixed doubles SL3-SU5 alongside Thulasimathi Murugesan.Naveen, meanwhile, defeated Indonesia's Fredy Setiawan 21-9, 21-17 to win the men's singles SL4 title. Thulasimathi enjoyed a memorable campaign of her own , combining with Manasi Joshi to win gold in women's doubles SL3-SU5. The Indian pair beat China's Yang Qiuxia and Xiao Zuxian 21-16, 21-13 in the final.The 24-year-old also secured silver in women's singles SU5 after losing 18-21, 11-21 to Yang in the final, completing a three-medal haul.Shooter Mona Agarwal added another golden chapter to India's campaign, shattering the world record to win the women's 50m rifle 3 positions SH1 title with a score of 357.5 points.The 38-year-old had earlier won the women's 10m air rifle standing SH1 gold with a Games-record score of 250.0 points, edging compatriot Avani Lekhara, who took silver with 249.6.Mona's latest triumph gave her a second gold of the Games and further underlined her standing among India's leading para-shooters. She had also secured India's first 2028 Paralympic quota earlier this year.In archery, Paralympic champion Harvinder Singh teamed up with debutant Vijay Sundi to win the men's recurve doubles gold, defeating China's Yun Duo and Zhao Lixue 5-1 in the final.India's women's recurve doubles pair of Bhawna Choudhary and Pooja Jatyan settled for silver after losing 0-6 to China's Gao Zihan and Wang Xueqian.India's swimmers also exceeded expectations, finishing the Games with 11 medals, including three silver. Himanshu Nandal completed a hat-trick of bronze medals by finishing third in the men's 100m freestyle S11. The 22-year-old, who was born blind due to optic nerve failure, clocked 1:05.90, behind Japan's Uchu Tomita (58.22) and China's Chuanzhen Sun (58.70).Nandal had earlier won bronze in the men's 400m freestyle and 100m breaststroke S11 events. Ravi Budigina also finished with three medals, comprising two silver and one bronze.With nine gold medals on Friday and a record overall haul of 114, India signed off from its Asian Para Games campaign with its most successful performance at the continental event, surpassing the benchmark set in Hangzhou three years ago.
Article Summary: India's para-athletes produced a spectacular finish to their campaign at the Asian Para Games. The country's final tally of 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze surpassed its previous best of 108 medals, including 27 gold, achieved at the Hangzhou Games in 2023. India's badminton contingent delivered three gold medals, led by Paris Paralympic champion Nitesh Kumar.

Article Title: Asian Para Games: Sumit Antil leads India's javelin 1-2-3 as Pranav Soorma strikes gold again

Sumit Antil and Pranav Soorma (ANI/PTI Photo)

Sumit Antil leads India's javelin sweep

Pranav Soorma defends club throw crown

NEW DELHI: India enjoyed a golden double in para-athletics at the Asian Para Games on Friday, with star javelin thrower Sumit Antil leading a podium sweep and Pranav Soorma defending his title in the men's club throw F51 event.Antil successfully defended his gold in the men's javelin throw F42-44/61-64 combined event, while Mahendra Gurjar and Sandip Sanjay Sargar completed an all-Indian podium finish. Soorma, meanwhile, added another gold to his collection with a Games-record performance in the club throw.The results added to India's medal haul as the country's para-athletes continued to deliver strong performances in Aichi-Nagoya.The 28-year-old Antil, a two-time Paralympic gold medallist and world record holder, produced a best throw of 72.46m in his second attempt to claim gold.Although he could not surpass his personal best, Antil was comfortably ahead of the field while competing in the F64 classification. He had won gold at the 2023 Asian Para Games with a then-world-record throw of 73.29m before improving the mark to 74.82m in May this year.Gurjar secured silver with a throw of 59.03m, while Sargar took bronze with an effort of 64.48m.Despite Sargar recording the longer distance, Gurjar finished ahead because of his superior Raza points score, which is used to determine rankings in combined events involving athletes from different classifications.The F42, F44, F62 and F64 categories are combined in certain field events, including javelin and discus throw, to create a larger and more competitive field. The classifications cover athletes with lower-limb impairments, with some competing without prostheses and others using them.Soorma continued India's gold rush by successfully defending his men's club throw F51 title with a Games-record effort of 32.87m.The Indian had won gold in the same event at the previous edition of the Asian Para Games and claimed silver at the 2024 Paris Paralympics.South Korea's Jiwon Jung took silver with a personal-best throw of 28.40m, while Dharamvir secured bronze with 27.71m to give India another double podium finish.The F51 classification is for athletes with significant movement limitations affecting the trunk, legs and hands, with varying degrees of impairment in arm movement. Competitors perform their throws from a seated position.With Antil leading a historic Indian sweep in the javelin and Soorma retaining his title, India's para-athletes delivered another memorable day in Aichi-Nagoya.

Article Title: Who is Himanshu Nandal? The para-swimmer who won a hat-trick of bronze medals at Asian Para Games in Japan
Article Text:
Himanshu Nandal (PTI Photo)

Who is Himanshu Nandal?

From Paris Paralympics qualification to Asian Para Games medals

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Indian para-swimmer Himanshu Nandal made his mark at the Asian Para Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, completing a hat-trick of bronze medals with another podium finish in the men's 100m freestyle S11 event on Friday.The 22-year-old clocked 1 minute 5.90 seconds to finish third, behind Japan's Uchu Tomita, who won gold in a Games-record time of 58.22 seconds, and China's Chuanzhen Sun, who took silver in 58.70 seconds.Nandal's latest medal added to his earlier bronze finishes in the men's 400m freestyle and 100m breaststroke S11 events. He became one of India's standout performers in para swimming, matching compatriot Ravi Budigina's three-medal haul at the Games, which comprised two silver medals and a bronze.Born blind due to optic nerve failure, Nandal grew up in a sports-oriented family in Rohtak, Haryana. His father had played hockey at the national level, and sport became part of his life from an early age.At four, Nandal moved to Delhi and joined the National Association for the Blind, where he learnt Braille. He initially took up judo and went on to win medals at the national level before switching to swimming in 2021.The change opened a new chapter in his sporting journey, as he quickly progressed from domestic competitions to the international stage.Nandal achieved a significant milestone in 2024 when he became the first Indian blind swimmer to meet the Minimum Qualification Standard for the Paris Paralympics.A political science graduate from the University of Delhi's Atma Ram Sanatan Dharma College, he continued to build his experience against international opposition. In 2025, he reached two finals at the World Para Swimming Championships in Singapore.At the Asian Para Games, Nandal began his medal-winning run on Tuesday, clocking 5:10.91 to secure bronze in the men's 400m freestyle S11 event. He followed it up with another third-place finish in the 100m breaststroke before completing his hat-trick in the 100m freestyle on Friday.The S11 classification is for swimmers with visual impairment, including those with very low visual acuity or no light perception.Nandal's three-medal campaign in Japan marks another milestone in his progress as an Indian para-swimmer and adds to his growing experience at major international competitions.
Article Summary: Himanshu Nandal completes hat-trick of bronze medals at Asian Para Games 2026. The 22-year-old finished third in the men's 100m freestyle S11 event on Friday. Nandal is the first Indian blind swimmer to meet the Minimum Qualification Standard for the Paris Paralympics.

NEW DELHI: Thulasimathi Murugesan produced a memorable triple-medal performance at the Asian Para Games 2026 on Friday, winning gold and two silver medals as India's para-badminton contingent enjoyed a productive day in Aichi-Nagoya.The 24-year-old Paris Paralympics silver medallist capped her campaign with gold in the women's doubles SL3-SU5 event, partnering Manasi Joshi to defeat China's Yang Qiuxia and Xiao Zuxian 21-16, 21-13 in the final. The Indian pair wrapped up the contest in just 28 minutes.Thulasimathi had earlier settled for silver in the women's singles SU5 final, losing 18-21, 11-21 to China's Yang. She then teamed up with Nitesh Kumar in the mixed doubles SL3-SU5 final, but the Indian combination went down 21-11, 19-21, 14-21 to Indonesia's Leani Ratri Oktila and Hikmat Ramdani.Nitesh, the Paris Paralympic champion, enjoyed a successful day of his own, winning gold in the men's singles SL3 event before adding mixed doubles silver with Thulasimathi.The 31-year-old defeated compatriot and Tokyo Paralympic gold medallist Pramod Bhagat 21-18, 21-16 in the men's singles final."Last time I was close, I was leading 19-16 in the third set, and then I lost. So this time, winning it and again winning in two sets against Pramod is, of course, very special, and I think it's one of the rarest of the rare things to see," Nitesh said after his victory.Naveen Sivakumar added another gold for India, beating Indonesia's Fredy Setiawan 21-9, 21-17 in the men's singles SL4 final. Paris Paralympic silver medallist defeats China's Yang Qiuxia and Xiao Zuxian 21-16, 21-13 in women's doubles final. Nitesh Kumar wins gold in men's singles SL3 event before adding mixed doubles silver. India's tally stands at 106 medals — 28 gold, 34 silver and 44 bronze — with country fourth in standings.

Article Title: Michael Carrick sacked as Manchester United head coach after just three wins in season
Article Text:
Manchester United's head coach Michael Carrick waves to supporters after his team lost the English Premier League football match between Manchester United and Bournemouth in Manchester, England, Sunday, Oct. 25, 2026. (AP Photo)

Michael Carrick has been sacked as Manchester United head coach, bringing an end to his 10-month spell in charge of the club, The Telegraph reported.The 45-year-old's departure comes after several days of uncertainty over his future, with United already working on appointing Mauricio Pochettino as his replacement. Carrick continued to take training on Tuesday and Wednesday before arriving at the club's Carrington training ground on Thursday morning, where he was finally informed of the decision.The decision to sack Carrick was approved at a meeting in Monaco on Wednesday involving co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox.However, it had become clear late on Monday that Carrick was set to leave. United spent the following days working on a deal to bring in Pochettino, the former Tottenham, Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain manager who is currently in charge of the United States national team.Pochettino is set to take charge of a United side struggling in the Premier League and the Champions League . The club are third from bottom of the Premier League, one point behind 17th-placed Coventry, and sit 17th in the Champions League standings.Carrick was appointed in May on a contract running until 2028 after a successful spell as interim manager.He had guided United to Champions League qualification, winning 12 and drawing three of his 17 matches last season. However, he was unable to maintain that record in the current campaign.United have managed only three wins in all competitions this season, against Ipswich, Sabah and Roma at home. They came back from two goals down to earn a late 4-4 draw against Aston Villa last Sunday. The team had also recovered to beat Roma, but the club's management decided that a change was necessary.Carrick's departure adds to the uncertainty surrounding United, where disagreements between senior players and club officials have also come into focus. Bruno Fernandes questioned Carrick's tactics following a 4-1 Champions League defeat against Como, while Martinez criticised Wilcox.Since Sir Alex Ferguson left the club in 2013, United have appointed eight managers, including Ralf Rangnick, who served as interim manager for five months.Carrick is the second United head coach to be sacked in the same calendar year. Ruben Amorim was dismissed in January, making this the first time in the club's history that two head coaches have been removed within one calendar year.
Article Summary: Michael Carrick has been sacked as Manchester United head coach. The 45-year- old's departure comes after several days of uncertainty over his future. United are already working on appointing Mauricio Pochettino as his replacement. The club are third from bottom of the Premier League, one point behind 17th-placed Coventry.

Article Title: How much will Manchester United pay to release Mauricio Pochettino and his coaching staff from USMNT to replace Michael Carrick?
Article Text:
Manchester United could face a $10 million release clause to prise current USMNT manager Mauricio Pochettino away from international football

Pochettino ’s USNMT release clause

The Athletic

Soccer Football - FIFA World Cup 2026 - Round of 16 - United States v Belgium - Seattle Stadium, Seattle, Washington, U.S. - July 6, 2026 U.S. coach Mauricio Pochettino speaks to the team after the match as the U.S. are eliminated from the World Cup REUTERS/Agustin Marcarian

Why Manchester United could pay the price

The Athletic

US Soccer has time to plan for a successor

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Mauricio Pochettino’s future with the United States men’s national team has become a subject of growing interest as Manchester United weigh up their next managerial appointment. Any move would involve more than persuading the Argentine to leave international football, however, with his existing contract carrying a significant financial commitment that could shape negotiations between the two organisations.The buyout clause in Mauricio Pochettino’s contract with US Soccer is understood to be in the region of $10 million, according to sources briefed on the situation who spoke to. Manchester United would be expected to consider the former Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea manager if they decide to replace Michael Carrick, and triggering that clause would give the Premier League club a route to securing Pochettino’s release from his national-team commitments.The cost would rise considerably if United also wanted to bring Pochettino’s coaching staff to Old Trafford. His assistants have followed him between clubs for more than a decade, and buying out their contracts would require several million dollars more, the sources said.A contractual buyout would provide US Soccer with a guaranteed starting point in negotiations and compensation that could be reinvested in appointing a successor.The federation, like other major football organisations, maintains a list of potential candidates in case a managerial change becomes necessary.The reported figure also gives an indication of the financial protection US Soccer secured when Pochettino agreed to extend his commitment. He had been free to leave when his previous arrangement reached the end of its term around the 2026 World Cup, but instead signed a new contract in August that runs through the 2030 tournament.That decision followed months of speculation about his long-term intentions. Pochettino has spoken openly about his ambition to manage in the Premier League again and his desire to win the competition, while acknowledging that he misses working in English football. Nevertheless, he insisted that his new agreement reflected a genuine commitment to the United States project.“Every time we sign a contract, it’s to go to the last day of the contract,” Pochettino said after returning. “If we sign a four-year contract, we need to think to arrive there. And we signed the contract because we really believe that we are going to be four years there. Because if not, it’s bad. If we don’t believe in that process, if we don’t believe in that journey, why (would) we sign four years? Only to be sure that we are going to receive a salary on the end of the month? That is not nice. It’s not the way that we think. We really signed that contract because we really believe that we can arrive to the end.”He added: “But in life, nothing is sure. Less in football.”Manchester United have not officially dismissed Carrick, but the club is expected to make a change, withreporting that Pochettino is among the leading candidates to take over. United have endured a difficult opening to the season, sitting 18th in the Premier League after collecting one win and eight points from their first 10 matches.Pochettino’s potential appointment would also revive a familiar managerial connection with English football. He previously managed Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea, and his record at Tottenham, where he reached the 2019 Champions League final, remains a significant part of his appeal.The financial terms would require United to consider not only the reported $10 million buyout for Pochettino but also the additional compensation necessary to secure his assistants. The total commitment could therefore run into the tens of millions of dollars before any salary package or other appointment costs are considered.For US Soccer, a departure would at least bring a financial return from a contract that might otherwise have ended without a buyout payment. The federation would also have time to identify a replacement, with the 2030 World Cup still several years away and qualifying for that tournament not scheduled to begin until next autumn.Pochettino remains with the USMNT squad at the national training centre in Fayetteville, Georgia, preparing for the Concacaf Nations League quarter-final against Haiti. The first leg is scheduled for Saturday in Miami, with the return match taking place next Tuesday in Cincinnati. He is expected to address the media on Friday, following his usual pre-match schedule.The immediate work comes during a period of transition for the national team after its elimination from the 2026 World Cup at the round-of-16 stage against Belgium. Since the tournament, Pochettino has begun introducing younger players into the senior squad, calling up 13 previously uncapped players across the September and October international windows. The United States won all four matches during that period.That development has given the federation an early foundation for the next World Cup cycle, although a change of manager would inevitably require a decision about whether to continue the direction established under Pochettino or appoint someone with a different approach.The timing would give US Soccer room to conduct that search. The team is still years away from the 2030 tournament, while its December camp is expected to be largely domestic-based and outside the FIFA international window. Its next competitive matches are scheduled for March, leaving the federation with a period in which it could assess candidates and negotiate an appointment.A Manchester United approach would therefore create a complicated decision for both sides. The United States has withdrawn from the upcoming Under-17 FIFA World Cup in Qatar over security concerns in the Middle East, according to US media reports on Wednesday.The decision was communicated to the players just over a week before the tournament begins on November 19, US Soccer Collective and The Athletic reported.US Soccer, the governing body of the sport in the United States, has not officially confirmed the withdrawal, news agency AFP reported.The decision comes amid the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, which began in February with joint US-Israeli strikes on Iran. Tehran retaliated by targeting several locations, including Gulf countries allied with Washington.Diplomatic efforts to end the conflict have continued, but the United States and Israel have repeatedly threatened to resume strikes on Iran.The conflict has also affected several sporting events in the region. The WTA Finals, which were scheduled to take place in Saudi Arabia, Qatar's neighbour, have been shifted to Indian Wells in the United States.This season's Formula One Grand Prix in Jeddah was cancelled, while the Bahrain race was also called off and later rescheduled under the same name in Malaysia. Several sporting events in Saudi Arabia have also been cancelled or postponed in recent weeks following attacks on the country by Yemen's Houthis.The United States were among the 48 teams scheduled to compete in the Under-17 World Cup. They had been placed in a group alongside Montenegro, Chile and Algeria.The Under-17 World Cup became an annual tournament last year and is being hosted by Qatar for five consecutive editions.When FIFA announced Qatar as the host for these tournaments in 2024, it said the decision to have one country host multiple editions was based on the opportunity to make "use of existing footballing infrastructure in the interest of tournament efficiencies and sustainability".Qatar had earlier hosted the 2022 men's FIFA World Cup.
Article Summary: The United States have withdrawn from the upcoming Under-17 FIFA World Cup in Qatar over security concerns in the Middle East. The decision was communicated to the players just over a week before the tournament begins on November 19. US Soccer, the governing body of the sport in the United States, has not officially confirmed the withdrawal.
